scene_objective: Setup phase, hook role: establish Ben's private crisis (the wrongness in the Force) as a concrete, embodied problem before any exposition names it. Ben loses a sparring exchange he should not have lost; the wrongness costs him a beat. Alone afterward, he stops pretending it is fatigue. The scene plants the central dramatic question (what is the wrongness, and why is Ben alone in perceiving it?) and positions Luke's arrival as the threshold into the main plot. Ben reads as a Knight handling a private problem privately—not performing a character arc in public.

turning_point.trigger: Alone in the salle, Ben runs a form through without igniting the blade and feels the wrongness steal a beat he cannot spare—a moment of muscle memory and Force timing that should be automatic, but isn't.
turning_point.shift: Ben stops pretending the wrongness is fatigue or residual disturbance from recent crises. He acknowledges, in the privacy of his own interiority, that something is structurally wrong with the Force itself, and that he is the only one feeling it.
turning_point.cost: The cost is isolation: Ben cannot unsee what he has felt, and he cannot explain it to the Order without sounding unreliable or traumatized. He is now carrying a secret he cannot share, and the weight of that silence begins here.

closing_beat: Luke appeared in the doorway with a datapad and an expression Ben knew meant a mission.

emotional_arc.start: Restless unease—Ben has been managing a low-level disturbance all week, attributing it to external noise or his own fatigue. The sparring loss sharpens the unease into something he cannot dismiss.
emotional_arc.shift: Frustrated isolation—alone in the salle, Ben tests the wrongness deliberately and feels it steal a beat he cannot spare. Frustration hardens into a kind of grim clarity: he is alone in this, and he knows it.
emotional_arc.end: Reluctant hope—Luke's arrival with a mission datapad offers a threshold. Ben does not yet know if Luke has sensed the wrongness or if this is coincidence, but the appearance of direction (a mission, a path forward) breaks the isolation of the preceding minutes.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben's guard drops a half-second late during a sparring exchange with a Knight, and the training blade catches him across the shoulder—the third time this week the wrongness has cost him a beat he should never miss.
key_beats.state_change: Ben is scored on, a concrete failure in a controlled environment. The wrongness has moved from private disturbance to public visibility.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's first impulse is to rationalize: fatigue, a long week, the ambient disturbance everyone has been attributing to post-Abeloth residue. But the rationalization does not settle. His body knows the difference between being tired and being interfered with. Beneath the surface calm, a sharp spike of something like fear—not fear of the sparring partner, but fear of what it means that his timing is fracturing.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben deactivates his training saber and waves off a rematch, claiming fatigue. The sparring partner accepts the excuse and leaves; Ben is alone in the salle.
key_beats.state_change: Ben has chosen not to name the wrongness aloud. He has chosen isolation over explanation. The salle empties, and Ben is left with the problem and no one to share it with.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Relief at the sparring partner's acceptance of the excuse, followed immediately by a hollow awareness that the relief is built on a lie. Ben's internal voice is sharp and self-deprecating—something like *that was convincing, at least*—but underneath is the knowledge that he is now committed to handling this alone.

key_beats.beat_description: Alone in the salle, Ben paces and then runs through a basic form without igniting the blade, testing whether the wrongness disrupts muscle memory or Force timing. Midway through the form, the wrongness pulls at his attention—a half-beat lag in the ambient field, the same lag he has felt all week but now undeniable.
key_beats.state_change: The wrongness is not fatigue. It is not external noise. It is structural. Ben can no longer pretend otherwise.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's body registers the lag before his mind articulates it—a subtle vertigo, a loss of the automatic synchronization between intention and execution that a trained Knight takes for granted. His breath catches. His next movement is deliberate, conscious, where it should be reflexive. The wrongness is not in his head; it is in the Force itself. And he is the only one who feels it. This realization arrives not as a thought but as a sensation: the cold clarity of being alone with something no one else can perceive.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben stops mid-form and stands still in the salle, breathing, the unignited blade hanging at his side. The ambient Force presence of the Temple—the hum of meditation chambers, the distant foot traffic of the late shift, the settled calm of the building—continues around him, indifferent.
key_beats.state_change: Ben has moved from testing the wrongness to accepting it. He is no longer trying to rationalize it away. He is standing in the center of the problem, alone.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The Temple's ambient presence, usually a comfort, now reads as a kind of blindness—all these Jedi, all this training, all this accumulated Force sensitivity, and none of them feel what Ben feels. The isolation is complete. But underneath the isolation is something else: a kind of grim determination. If no one else feels it, then no one else can help. Ben will have to figure this out alone. The thought does not comfort him, but it steadies him.

voice_guidance: Channel Zahn's efficient close third-person interiority—sharp, self-deprecating, never melodramatic. Ben's internal voice is precise and unsentimental; he observes his own reactions with a kind of wry distance. When the wrongness manifests, describe it through sensory and vibrational language, not visual or color terms. Use one consistent metaphor for this scene: the half-beat lag in the ambient field. Ben should not arrive at any clinical articulation of what the wrongness is—he feels it before he can name it. If a sentence of his interiority could be lifted into a mission debrief, it is too composed for this scene. The sparring partner is minimal—a professional presence, not a character. Temple life surfaces in the edges: late-shift foot traffic, the hum of meditation chambers, lift chimes in the corridor. Coruscant is a place people live in, not only a backdrop Ben moves through.
forbidden_moves: Do not open with a flashback or exposition about recent crises.
Do not describe the wrongness in visual or color terms—keep it auditory and vibrational.
Do not have Ben arrive at any clinical or diagnostic articulation of the wrongness in this scene.
Do not characterize the sparring partner beyond minimal professional presence.
Do not have Ben confide in or explain the wrongness to the sparring partner or any other Knight in this scene.
Do not use melodramatic or overwrought language for Ben's internal voice.
Do not shift the POV away from Ben or into the sparring partner's perspective.
